newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Cash support props up gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Cash support props up gas oil.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Wednesday on sustained physical support despite a big drop in crude prices, traders said.

"Gas oil is holding up well even though crude is down because of the continued physical purchases," one trader said. June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.80-$24.85 per barrel range while July was quoted at $24.80-$24.90, both down about five cents from Tuesday, brokers said.
June traded earlier in the day at $24.80 and July traded at $24.85 and $24.90 per barrel, they said.
Traders said the market withstood an overnight 78 cents drop in July Brent crude prices to $19.22 per barrel due to sustained buying from three traders.

The traders, who have bought over 20 million barrels of gas oil since March 3, purchased three 150,000-barrel cargoes at $25.00 and $25.10 per barrel free-on-board Singapore on Tuesday, up 20 and 30 cents above Monday's traded level.
The same traders also bought up to two million barrels of June and July swaps late last week which put a floor on prices at $24.70 per barrel for both months.

But market nervousness was reflected in the small contango that is developing between the front months of June and July at about five cents, compared to backwardation of over $1.00 less than a month ago.

Market jitters are due to the overwhelming number of sellers in the local spot market where over the past week, up to 10 cargoes have been offered daily with between one and four cargoes traded per day.
Traders said that the sellers are mainly made up of those who have not been able to offload their arbitrage cargoes.
June fuel oil was last quoted down about 75 cents from Tuesday at $99.00/$100.00 per tonne, brokers said. The weaker prices were due to both poor demand and the big drop to crude prices.
